MH03.answer_text: Kamrup Metropolitan has the most installer-attributed warranty claims — 602 claims (installer_claims metric), well ahead of Kolkata (373) and Patna (330). The reason is an installer, not a bad batch: the installer_scan anomaly detector flags installer INS0227, who works in Kamrup Metropolitan, with 139 claims against an expected ~52 (effect size 2.65, p≈2.9e-23) across 1,085 installs spanning 2 plants and 73 resin lots — a broad pattern inconsistent with a single defective lot. The lot_scan detector's strongest flag is resin lot RL-DGP-L2-250310 (base cracks, 291 claims vs ~76 expected), but it is not tied to Kamrup Metropolitan, so a bad production batch is not the supported explanation for that district's high claims.
sql:
SELECT
  install_district AS installer_cohort_month__install_district
  , SUM(claims) AS installer_claims
FROM "marts"."mart_installer_claim_cohorts" installer_claim_cohorts_src_10000
GROUP BY
  install_district
ORDER BY installer_claims DESC, installer_cohort_month__install_district
LIMIT 500

MH04.question: Why does channel stock tend to rise right after each quarter-end?
MH04.answer_text: Channel stock (channel_stock_units) climbs in the last two weeks of each fiscal quarter and then unwinds: e.g. it rose from ~1.91M units in the week of 2026-02-23 to ~2.50M by 2026-03-30, and from ~1.84M to ~2.25M into the March 2025 quarter-end. The pre-registered stuffing detector flags this as quarter-end channel stuffing — distributors ordering well above their trailing-90-day rate in the scheme window (last 15 days), with 280 distributor-category flags in FY26Q4 and 276 in FY25Q4 (stuffing_flags metric). So the post-quarter-end stock build-up is driven by scheme-window order loading ahead of quarter close, not by a change in sell-out.
sql:
SELECT
  subq_5.metric_time__week AS metric_time__week
  , SUM(subq_5.__channel_stock_units) AS channel_stock_units
FROM (
  SELECT
    channel_stock_units AS __channel_stock_units
    , week_start__week
    , metric_time__week
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS week_start__week
      , DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS metric_time__week
      , days_of_stock is not null AS inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
      , stock_units AS channel_stock_units
    FROM "marts"."mart_channel_inventory_weekly" channel_inventory_src_10000
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) BETWEEN '2026-01-26' AND '2026-04-05'
  ) subq_4
  WHERE inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
) subq_5
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    metric_time__week
    , MAX(week_start__week) AS week_start__week__complete
  FROM (
    SELECT
      DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS week_start__week
      , DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) AS metric_time__week
      , days_of_stock is not null AS inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
    FROM "marts"."mart_channel_inventory_weekly" channel_inventory_src_10000
    WHERE DATE_TRUNC('week', week_start) BETWEEN '2026-01-26' AND '2026-04-05'
  ) subq_4
  WHERE inventory_week__has_days_of_stock
  GROUP BY
    metric_time__week
) subq_7
ON
  subq_5.week_start__week = subq_7.week_start__week__complete
GROUP BY
  subq_5.metric_time__week
ORDER BY metric_time__week
LIMIT 500

response.answer_text: Channel stock (channel_stock_units) climbs in the last two weeks of each fiscal quarter and then unwinds: e.g. it rose from ~1.91M units in the week of 2026-02-23 to ~2.50M by 2026-03-30, and from ~1.84M to ~2.25M into the March 2025 quarter-end. The pre-registered stuffing detector flags this as quarter-end channel stuffing — distributors ordering well above their trailing-90-day rate in the scheme window (last 15 days), with 280 distributor-category flags in FY26Q4 and 276 in FY25Q4 (stuffing_flags metric). So the post-quarter-end stock build-up is driven by scheme-window order loading ahead of quarter close, not by a change in sell-out.

  , SUM(__stuffing_flags) AS stuffing_flags
FROM (

    fiscal_quarter_label AS distributor_scheme_window__fiscal_quarter_label

  FROM "marts"."mart_scheme_quarterly" scheme_quarterly_src_10000

) subq_5

ORDER BY stuffing_flags DESC, distributor_scheme_window__fiscal_quarter_label
LIMIT 500

with params as (
    select coalesce(NULL::date, (select max(snapshot_date) from marts.mart_anomaly_flags)) as as_of
),
latest as (
    select distinct on (f.detector, f.entity_type, f.entity_id, f.failure_mode, f.details ->> 'category') f.*
    from marts.mart_anomaly_flags f, params p
    where f.snapshot_date <= p.as_of
    order by f.detector, f.entity_type, f.entity_id, f.failure_mode, f.details ->> 'category', f.snapshot_date desc
)
select p.as_of, l.detector, l.entity_type, l.entity_id, l.failure_mode, l.region, l.snapshot_date,
       l.first_flag_date, l.effect_size, l.p_value, l.details
from latest l, params p
where l.first_flag_date <= p.as_of
  and ('stuffing'::text is null or l.detector = 'stuffing')
  and (NULL::text is null or l.failure_mode = NULL)
-- Strongest first within each detector, interleaved across detectors (D34): the model reads only the first rows, so
-- one detector's long list must not push the others out of view.
order by row_number() over (partition by l.detector order by l.effect_size desc nulls last, l.entity_id, l.failure_mode),
         l.detector
